tools.description: Author 1–50 tickets and up to 100 links in one all-or-nothing write. Each ticket carries a batch-local `ref`; a link end is a ref or an existing ticket (`from_id` / `to_id`; a from_id needs its claim_token in `claims`). Rejected as a whole on duplicate refs, unknown refs or ids, self-loops, duplicate links, or a parent_of/depends_on/blocks cycle across existing links — the error lists every problem. `dry_run` validates only.

dry_run.description: Validate and report what would happen; write nothing.

tools.description: Take a lease on one or more tickets (all-or-nothing; locked in id order so concurrent claimers cannot deadlock). Returns one claim_token per ticket — keep it, it is shown once and is required for every write. Leases (default 900 s, max 3600 s) renew while you keep calling sea-lite tools; otherwise they lapse. Fails with already_claimed (naming the holder and expiry) if any ticket is held by someone else. Claiming a ticket you already hold rotates its token. Pass `scope.paths` (the files or directories you will edit; a worktree is a scope) to lock them for the lease: refused with scope_conflict, naming the holder, ticket, overlapping paths and expiry, if they overlap someone else's live scope (another actor, or this actor in another session).

actor_id.description: Who is calling. Defaults to the server --actor. Claims are held per actor; subagents sharing one server should each pass their own.

lease_seconds.description: Lease length in seconds (default 900, max 3600). Renewed automatically while you keep calling sea-lite tools; expiry frees the ticket.

scope.description: The files you are going to touch (paths and/or worktree). Refused with scope_conflict if any path overlaps a live claim held by someone else (another actor, or this actor in another session).

paths.description: Repo-relative paths. A plain path locks itself and everything beneath it; a glob (picomatch: `*` within a segment, `**` across) locks what it matches; `.` is the whole repo.

worktree.description: Absolute path of the git worktree you work in. Binds the claim to it: `sea-lite release-worktree <path>` frees it when the worktree is removed.

ticket_ids.description: One or more tickets. All are claimed or none is.

tools.description: Create one ticket (status idea, or triaged to make it dispatchable right away). Returns the ticket plus `possible_duplicates` — existing tickets with the same or a similar title; the create always goes through, you decide. Pass `claim_seconds` to claim it in the same call and get a claim_token back. `idempotency_key` makes retries safe. Kinds: feature | research | investigation | refactor | curiosity | question | other | bug | chore | incident | security | epic | spike | log | docs | decision. Priorities: urgent | high | medium | low | parked.

tools.description: Add or remove a directed link `from <link_type> to`. Types: parent_of | relates_to | inspired_by | responds_to | conflicts_with | supersedes | blocks | depends_on | condenses_into | branches_from | references | duplicates. Fenced on the from ticket (claim_token). parent_of / depends_on / blocks are kept acyclic across all existing links; a cycle is rejected with its path. Remove tombstones the link (history keeps it). `from blocks to` and `from depends_on to` decide what sea_next may hand out: a ticket is eligible only when every predecessor is terminal.

tools.description: Dispatch: atomically pick and claim the highest-priority unclaimed triaged or in_progress ticket that is assigned to you or unassigned, is not priority parked, and whose predecessors (tickets that `blocks` it, tickets it `depends_on`) are all terminal. in_progress beats triaged at equal priority; then oldest (chain order) first. Returns ticket + claim_token, or ticket: null with reason nothing_eligible. This project only. Call it in a loop. `scope.paths` locks the paths you will edit for the lease (scope_conflict if they overlap someone else's live scope).

tools.title: Per-actor claim accounting

tools.description: Set status. Fenced (claim_token). Legal moves: work track idea → triaged → in_progress → resolved; any active ticket may enter parked | blocked | needs_decision (resume only to idea / triaged / in_progress) or a terminal state resolved | wont_fix | duplicate | dropped | merged (no exit). to=duplicate requires duplicate_of and records a `duplicates` link. Entering a terminal state releases your claim and asks for confirmation unless confirm: true is passed. On rejection the error carries legal_next. Known statuses: idea | triaged | in_progress | in_design | ready | parked | blocked | needs_decision | resolved | wont_fix | duplicate | dropped | merged.

actor_id.description: Who is calling. Defaults to the server --actor. Claims are held per actor; subagents sharing one server should each pass their own.

claim_token.description: The claim token returned by sea_claim or sea_next.

confirm.description: Terminal states (resolved | wont_fix | duplicate | dropped | merged) have no exit. Pass true to enter one directly. When omitted, a client that supports elicitation is asked to confirm (input_required); one that does not gets confirmation_required.

dry_run.description: Validate and report what would happen; write nothing.

duplicate_of.description: Required when to = duplicate; also creates a `duplicates` link.

expected_version.description: Optimistic concurrency: fail with version_conflict unless the ticket row_version equals this.

idempotency_key.description: Replay-safe key. A second call with the same key returns the first result without writing again.
